value.name: Lucia agrees to Sunday dinners
value.description: Lucia explains that she told him he can come for dinner on Sundays and that he must be polite to Rosa, and he agreed to try.
evidence: "I told him he can come for dinner on Sundays. I told him Rosa will sometimes be here and he will have to be polite to her, and he said he would be. He may not be, every Sunday. But he said he would try."

value.name: Asha acknowledges the arrangement
value.description: Asha responds approvingly to Lucia's update about the dinner arrangement.

value.name: Lucia thanks Asha for letting them decide
value.description: Lucia thanks Asha for not deciding for them and for making them decide for themselves.
evidence: "Asha." Lucia hesitated. "Thank you. I know that is what people say. I mean it differently. Thank you for not deciding for us. Thank you for making us decide."

value.name: Asha deflects praise as her job
value.description: Asha says that allowing others to decide is simply her job.

value.name: Lucia challenges lawyers' behavior
value.description: Lucia says that lawyers do not always behave the way Asha does and implies Asha's approach is unusual.
evidence: "It is not always the job. I have watched lawyers before. It is not always the job."

value.name: Asha falls silent
value.description: Asha does not know how to respond to Lucia's remark and says nothing.
evidence: Asha did not know what to say to that, so she said nothing.

value.name: Rosa serves Asha coffee
value.description: Rosa silently places a cup of coffee in front of Asha without asking, continuing her long-standing routine in the kitchen.
evidence: Rosa set a cup of coffee in front of her. She had not asked if Asha wanted one. She had simply made it, the way she had made coffee in this kitchen for thirty-one years, and she set it down and went back to the stove.

value.name: Asha drinks the coffee
value.description: Asha drinks the coffee Rosa made and finds it excellent.
evidence: Asha drank the coffee. It was very good.

value.name: Asha pauses at the doorway
value.description: On her way out, Asha stops on the stoop as she had on her first day, taking in the spring afternoon and the sounds of the neighborhood.
evidence: At the door, on her way out, she stopped on the stoop the way she had stopped on her first day.
The rain was long gone. The block was full of the small loud sounds of an afternoon in spring, a child on a bicycle, someone's radio, a delivery truck idling at the corner.

value.name: Lucia and Rosa begin talking comfortably
value.description: Asha hears Lucia and Rosa talking in a relaxed, familiar way that shows they now live together without fear.
evidence: through it she could hear Lucia and Rosa beginning to talk about something in the low easy register of two people who lived in the same house now, in different ways, and who had finally, after a long winter, stopped being afraid of each other.

value.name: Asha leaves feeling lighter
value.description: Asha walks away toward Walnut Street with the file under her arm feeling lighter as she heads home.
evidence: She went down the three stone steps and turned toward Walnut Street, the file under her arm gone light, and she walked home
